rationale: The SKILL.md is mostly an install pointer to an external GitHub repo (git-fetch a pinned commit into ~/.claude/skills) whose detection strength targets C++/Android/iOS/Web vendoring; Python projects declare deps in pyproject.toml, so the embedded-library problem this solves rarely exists in this developer's stack, and adopting an unaudited external tool for a hypothetical legacy-takeover scenario fails the smallest-durable-pattern bar.
overlap_with_existing: None direct; ad-hoc repo exploration plus the cost-estimate skill cover the occasional 'understand a foreign codebase' need.
evidence_notes: Read reference_harnesses/everything-claude-code/skills/repo-scan/SKILL.md (81 lines): install-from-github block, capability/depth tables, 5-step how-it-works, C++ monorepo example. Actual logic lives in the external haibindev/repo-scan repo, not the skill.

name: request-refactor-plan
fable_reason: Deprecated; refactor planning useful but redundant with existing planning skills.
gpt_reason: Generic incremental refactor planning and GitHub issue capture.
description: Create a detailed refactor plan with tiny commits via user interview, then file it as a GitHub issue. Use when user wants to plan a refactor, create a refactoring RFC, or break a refactor into safe incremental steps.
problem_solved: Interview-driven refactor planning: verify the user's claims against the repo, hammer out scope and test coverage, break work into tiny always-green commits (Fowler discipline), and file the plan as a GitHub issue with a decision-document template.
rationale: Decent template (decision doc, testing decisions, out-of-scope, no-file-paths durability rule), but upstream deprecated it and every element is already covered locally: brainstorming does the interview, planning produces the durable plan, document-review critiques it, and Beads is the filing target instead of GitHub issues; the one nugget - explicit tiny-always-green-commit sequencing - is a line for planning guidance, not a skill.
overlap_with_existing: brainstorming + planning + document-review skills; Beads replaces the gh issue sink; grill-me covers the adversarial-interview angle.
evidence_notes: Read reference_harnesses/mattpocock_skills/skills/deprecated/request-refactor-plan/SKILL.md (69 lines): 8-step interview flow, refactor-plan issue template. Upstream 'deprecated' bucket per their CLAUDE.md.

name: santa-method
fable_reason: Dual-agent adversarial verification is generic but heavyweight; redundant with existing review loops.
gpt_reason: Generic adversarial multi-agent verification, but heavyweight for routine work.
description: Multi-agent adversarial verification with convergence loop. Two independent review agents must both pass before output ships.
problem_solved: Post-generation verification gate: two context-isolated reviewer agents score output against an objective rubric, both must pass, failed rounds feed a bounded fix loop (max 3) with fresh reviewers each round, plus a batch-sampling variant for large generations.
rationale: Well-articulated (rubric-design table, failure-mode mitigations, fresh-reviewers-per-round to kill anchoring), but the core problem - breaking self-review bias via an independent second reviewer - is already solved locally with genuine model diversity: use-codex/codex-review gives a cross-model adversarial pass, and code-review's higher effort levels run multi-agent; two same-model reviewers are a weaker form of what we run today, so park it unless a batch-content-generation workload appears where the sampling pattern earns its cost.
overlap_with_existing: use-codex + codex-adapter:codex-review (cross-model independent critic), code-review skill (multi-agent at high/ultra effort), verification-before-completion (evidence gate).
evidence_notes: Read reference_harnesses/everything-claude-code/skills/santa-method/SKILL.md (308 lines): 4-phase architecture, reviewer prompt, rubric tables, convergence loop with MAX_ITERATIONS=3, batch sampling, failure-mode table, cost analysis.
